description: Use case runner scenarios (write-path contract sections 3a, 4, 4a, 5). Setup: aggregate table thing(id text primary key, client_id text, version bigint, name text, code text UNIQUE); rows are written as 'id|client|version|name|code' ('-' = null code). Command: op (create | edit | remove | emit), id, name, code; create inserts a new thing (version 0 -> 1), edit changes name and/or code of the thing found, remove deletes it, emit plans an event only. useCase: validate/authorize = ok | refuse (an error of kind VALIDATION / AUTHORIZATION) | throw (an exception whose message must never reach the error); load = none | ok (finds the thing by id, scoped to the context's client) | throw; whenMissing is NOT_FOUND THING_NOT_FOUND; authorizeLoaded = none | ok (refuses a thing named 'locked' with AUTHORIZATION LOCKED) | refuse (always AUTHORIZATION LOCKED) | hide (answers whenMissing) | throw; execute = edit | create | remove | emit | reject (BUSINESS_RULE REJECTED) | throw | crossClient / crossClientDelete (a plan holding a thing of client 'other') | createThenClash (saves two things, the second violating the unique code); without a load phase edit/remove find the thing themselves (trace 'find'). conflict = fail | retry (maxAttempts, backoff 5 ms, jittered 0.5x to 1.5x). faults: concurrentWrite (another writer bumps the row's version after the attempt loaded it, so the update affects 0 rows) | sqlState (the update throws an SQLException with that SQLSTATE) | persistError (any other exception in the persist step) | events | audit (the sink throws) | commitTrigger (a deferred constraint fails at COMMIT) | begin (the database cannot give a connection) | interrupt (the wait between attempts is interrupted); attempts = the 1-based attempts the fault applies to. join: null runs in the runner's own transaction; else the runner is handed the caller's connection (autoCommit false unless stated), callerInsert writes the row mine|acme|1|callers|C-1 in it first, end = commit | rollback, followUp = a further command run on the same transaction after the first. expect: result committed | failed; error {kind, code, httpStatus, details} (message is Java's wording in messageJava and is not compared; a cause's text never appears in it); trace = the phases called, in order, across all attempts; attempts = how many attempts ran; waits = how many waits between attempts; events = [{type, subject}] the sink received (committed work only); audits = [{entityType, entityId, operation}]; things = the aggregate rows after the scenario ('id|client|version|name|code'); for a join: seenByOthersBeforeEnd = rows another connection sees while the caller's transaction is open, and followUp the result of the second run; throws = the exception class name when the run is an argument error. Outbox rows proper are covered by outbox/outbox.json; here the sink's events stand for them.
howToRun: Per scenario: reset the database, create the table, insert prior, build the use case from 'useCase', inject the faults, run it with the context (client, principal usr_1) and the command (joined or not), then compare the expect block. Regenerate from Java with -Dconformance.update=true (UseCaseScenariosConformanceTest).
